label: Silas
note: Companion of Paul on the second journey (from Acts 15:22, a leading man of the Jerusalem assembly); shares the Philippi beating and imprisonment (Acts 16:19-40).

label: Timothy of Lystra
note: Disciple from Lystra; son of a believing Jewish mother and a Greek father (Acts 16:1); circumcised by Paul and joined the journey (16:3). No source outside the New Testament names him.

label: Acts 17:1
text: Now when they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.

label: Acts 17:2
text: Paul, as was his custom, went in to them, and for three Sabbath days reasoned with them from the Scriptures,

label: Acts 17:3
text: explaining and demonstrating that the Christ had to suffer and rise again from the dead, and saying, “This Jesus, whom I proclaim to you, is the Christ.”

label: Acts 17:4
text: Some of them were persuaded, and joined Paul and Silas, of the devout Greeks a great multitude, and not a few of the chief women.

label: Acts 17:5
text: But the unpersuaded Jews took along some wicked men from the marketplace, and gathering a crowd, set the city in an uproar. Assaulting the house of Jason, they sought to bring them out to the people.

label: Acts 17:6
text: When they didn’t find them, they dragged Jason and certain brothers before the rulers of the city, crying, “These who have turned the world upside down have come here also,

label: Acts 17:7
text: whom Jason has received. These all act contrary to the decrees of Caesar, saying that there is another king, Jesus!”

label: Acts 17:8
text: The multitude and the rulers of the city were troubled when they heard these things.

label: Acts 17:9
text: When they had taken security from Jason and the rest, they let them go.

label: Acts 17:10
text: The brothers immediately sent Paul and Silas away by night to Beroea. When they arrived, they went into the Jewish synagogue.

label: Acts 17:11
text: Now these were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, examining the Scriptures daily to see whether these things were so.

label: Acts 17:12
text: Many of them therefore believed; also of the prominent Greek women, and not a few men.

label: Acts 17:13
text: But when the Jews of Thessalonica had knowledge that the word of God was proclaimed by Paul at Beroea also, they came there likewise, agitating the multitudes.

label: Acts 17:14
text: Then the brothers immediately sent out Paul to go as far as to the sea, and Silas and Timothy still stayed there.

label: Acts 17:15
text: But those who escorted Paul brought him as far as Athens. Receiving a commandment to Silas and Timothy that they should come to him very quickly, they departed.

label: Acts 17:16
text: Now while Paul waited for them at Athens, his spirit was provoked within him as he saw the city full of idols.

label: Acts 17:17
text: So he reasoned in the synagogue with the Jews and the devout persons, and in the marketplace every day with those who met him.

variants.note: Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles' lists Acts 17:26 'ex henos' in P74, Sinaiticus, A, B, 33, 81, 181, 629, 630, 1739, vg, cop sa, bo; 'ex henos aimatos' in D, E, P, 049, 056, 0142, 88, 104, 326, 330, 436, 451, 614, 945, 1241, 1505, 1877, 2127, 2412, 2492, 2495, Byz, Lect; 'ex henos stomatos' in Psi, l 603.

label: Acts 17:18
text: Some of the Epicurean and Stoic philosophers also were conversing with him. Some said, “What does this babbler want to say?” Others said, “He seems to be advocating foreign deities,” because he preached Jesus and the resurrection.

label: Acts 17:19
text: They took hold of him, and brought him to the Areopagus, saying, “May we know what this new teaching is, which is spoken by you?

label: Acts 17:20
text: For you bring certain strange things to our ears. We want to know therefore what these things mean.”

label: Acts 17:21
text: Now all the Athenians and the strangers living there spent their time in nothing else, but either to tell or to hear some new thing.

label: Acts 17:22
text: Paul stood in the middle of the Areopagus, and said, “You men of Athens, I perceive that you are very religious in all things.

label: Acts 17:23
text: For as I passed along, and observed the objects of your worship, I found also an altar with this inscription: ‘TO AN UNKNOWN GOD.’ What therefore you worship in ignorance, this I announce to you.

label: Acts 17:24
text: The God who made the world and all things in it, he, being Lord of heaven and earth, doesn’t dwell in temples made with hands,

label: Acts 17:25
text: neither is he served by men’s hands, as though he needed anything, seeing he himself gives to all life and breath, and all things.

label: Acts 17:26
text: He made from one blood every nation of men to dwell on all the surface of the earth, having determined appointed seasons, and the boundaries of their dwellings,

label: Acts 17:27
text: that they should seek the Lord, if perhaps they might reach out for him and find him, though he is not far from each one of us.

label: Acts 17:28
text: ‘For in him we live, and move, and have our being.’ As some of your own poets have said, ‘For we are also his offspring.’

label: Acts 17:29
text: Being then the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Divine Nature is like gold, or silver, or stone, engraved by art and design of man.

label: Acts 17:30
text: The times of ignorance therefore God overlooked. But now he commands that all people everywhere should repent,

label: Acts 17:31
text: because he has appointed a day in which he will judge the world in righteousness by the man whom he has ordained; of which he has given assurance to all men, in that he has raised him from the dead.”

label: Acts 17:32
text: Now when they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some mocked; but others said, “We want to hear you again concerning this.”

label: Acts 17:33
text: Thus Paul went out from among them.

label: Acts 17:34
text: But certain men joined with him, and believed, among whom also was Dionysius the Areopagite, and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.

label: Wikipedia: Politarch

label: Ploughboy Blog: To the Unknown Gods (quoting G. A. Barton, Archaeology and the New Testament)

label: Wikipedia: Areopagus
title: Areopagus
excerpt: The Areopagus Council continued to function as a body of former archons in Roman times. After Sulla's capture of Athens in 86/87 BC and subsequent restructuring of the city's political structure, it was elevated to one of the most prestigious and politically powerful institutions in Athens.

label: Wikipedia: Amphipolis
title: Amphipolis

label: Wikipedia: Beroea
title: Beroea
excerpt: Within the city there was a Jewish settlement in which Paul, [ 4 ] after he had left Thessalonica , and his companion, Silas , preached to the Jewish and Greek communities of the city in AD 50/51 or 54/55.

label: Wikipedia: Thessaloniki

label: Jason of Thessalonica
note: Host in Thessalonica who was dragged before the politarchs (17:5-9); 'Jason my kinsman' of Romans 16:21 is traditionally identified with him; venerated as a saint (reception, not independent evidence).

label: Dionysius the Areopagite
note: Member of the Areopagus who believed at Athens (17:34). Known only from Acts; later tradition makes him first (or second) bishop of Athens, and the 5th-6th-century 'Pseudo-Dionysius' corpus was written under his name.

label: Damaris
note: Woman who believed at Athens (17:34); mentioned nowhere else in the New Testament.

label: Apollonia of Mygdonia
modern_name: near Nea Apollonia, Central Macedonia, Greece

label: Areopagus (Hill of Ares), Athens
periods: Archaic to Roman; council of former archons, homicide court and religious tribunal

label: Paul and his company passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia to Thessalonica
statement: Paul and his companions passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia and came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.

label: Thessalonica had a Jewish synagogue
statement: There was a Jewish synagogue in Thessalonica when Paul arrived.
note: Jewish presence in Beroea is also stated at 17:10; diaspora synagogue life is attested as a class by claim:ac-13-16-god-fearers and its evidence (Miletus, Aphrodisias).

label: Paul reasoned in the synagogue on three Sabbath days, as was his custom
statement: Paul, as was his custom, went in to the Thessalonian synagogue and for three Sabbath days reasoned with them from the Scriptures.

label: Paul taught that the Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead
statement: Paul explained and demonstrated from the Scriptures that the Christ had to suffer and rise again from the dead, and said this Jesus is the Christ.

label: Devout Greeks and prominent women joined Paul and Silas in Thessalonica
statement: Some were persuaded and joined Paul and Silas, including a great multitude of the devout Greeks and not a few of the chief women.

label: A mob from the marketplace assaulted Jason's house in Thessalonica
statement: Unpersuaded Jews took wicked men from the marketplace, gathered a crowd, set the city in an uproar and assaulted the house of Jason, seeking Paul and Silas.

label: Thessalonica's city magistrates were called 'rulers of the city' (politarchai)
statement: Jason and certain brothers were dragged before the 'rulers of the city' (Greek politarchai); the multitude and the rulers of the city were troubled. The title appears twice, at 17:6 and 17:8.

label: Jason and certain brothers were dragged before the city magistrates
statement: When the mob did not find Paul and Silas, they dragged Jason and certain brothers before the rulers of the city.

label: Jason was accused of acting contrary to Caesar's decrees and of another king, Jesus
statement: The accusers charged that Jason had received the missionaries, that 'these all act contrary to the decrees of Caesar, saying that there is another king, Jesus'.

label: The magistrates took security (bond) from Jason and the rest and let them go
statement: The Thessalonican magistrates took security (a bond or pledge) from Jason and the rest and let them go.

label: The brothers sent Paul and Silas away by night to Beroea
statement: The brothers immediately sent Paul and Silas away by night to Beroea, where they went into the Jewish synagogue.

label: Beroea had a Jewish synagogue
statement: When Paul and Silas arrived in Beroea they went into the Jewish synagogue.

label: The Beroeans examined the Scriptures daily
statement: The Beroeans received the word with all readiness of mind, examining the Scriptures daily to see whether these things were so.

label: Many in Beroea believed, including prominent Greek women and men
statement: Many of the Beroeans believed, including prominent Greek women and not a few men.

label: Jews from Thessalonica came to Beroea and agitated the crowds
statement: When the Jews of Thessalonica learned the word was proclaimed at Beroea, they came there likewise, agitating the multitudes.

label: The brothers sent Paul toward the sea while Silas and Timothy stayed in Beroea
statement: The brothers immediately sent Paul out to go as far as to the sea; Silas and Timothy still stayed in Beroea.

label: Paul was escorted to Athens; Silas and Timothy were summoned
statement: Those who escorted Paul brought him as far as Athens and departed with a commandment that Silas and Timothy should come to him very quickly.

label: Athens was full of idols when Paul waited there
statement: While Paul waited at Athens, his spirit was provoked within him as he saw the city full of idols (kateidolos).

label: Paul reasoned daily in the synagogue and the marketplace of Athens
statement: Paul reasoned in the synagogue with the Jews and the devout persons, and in the marketplace (agora) every day with those who met him.

label: Epicurean and Stoic philosophers conversed with Paul in Athens
statement: Some of the Epicurean and Stoic philosophers were conversing with Paul in Athens; some called him a babbler (spermologos) and others said he advocated foreign deities.

label: Paul was accused of advocating foreign deities because he preached Jesus and the resurrection
statement: The philosophers said, 'He seems to be advocating foreign deities,' because he preached Jesus and the resurrection - to Greek ears anastasis (resurrection) could sound like a goddess.

label: Paul was taken hold of and brought to the Areopagus
statement: The philosophers took hold of Paul and brought him to the Areopagus, asking what this new teaching was that he spoke.

label: The Areopagus was the Athenian council that could examine new teaching
statement: The Areopagus functioned in Paul's Athens as a council of former archons and a prestigious body that examined a teacher of 'certain strange things to our ears'.

label: Athenians and residents spent their time telling or hearing something new
statement: All the Athenians and the strangers living there spent their time in nothing else but either to tell or to hear some new thing.

label: Paul stood in the middle of the Areopagus
statement: Paul stood in the middle of the Areopagus and addressed 'You men of Athens'.
note: Whether this means the council body or the physical hill is disputed; see the complicates edge on site:areopagus.

label: An altar inscribed 'TO AN UNKNOWN GOD' existed in Athens
statement: As Paul passed along and observed the objects of worship at Athens, he found an altar with the inscription 'TO AN UNKNOWN GOD' (agnosto theo).

label: Paul taught that God does not dwell in temples made with hands
statement: In the Areopagus speech Paul taught that the God who made the world does not dwell in temples made with hands, nor is he served by men's hands as though he needed anything.

label: Paul taught that God made every nation from one man and set their seasons and boundaries
statement: In the speech Paul taught that God made 'from one blood every nation of men' to dwell on the whole surface of the earth, having determined appointed seasons and the boundaries of their dwellings.

label: Paul quoted 'in him we live and move and have our being'
statement: In the speech Paul quoted, 'For in him we live, and move, and have our being', attributed by many commentators to Epimenides of Crete.
note: The Epimenides attribution is disputed: no extant manuscript of Epimenides contains the phrase; it is reconstructed by Rendel Harris from a Syriac commentary.

label: Paul quoted 'For we are also his offspring' (Aratus, Phaenomena 5)
statement: Paul continued, 'As some of your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring' - the line of Aratus's Phaenomena, line 5.

label: Paul taught that the Divine Nature is not like gold, silver or stone images
statement: In the speech Paul argued that, being the offspring of God, we ought not to think the Divine Nature is like gold, silver or stone, engraved by art and design of man.

label: Paul taught a appointed day of judgment by the man God raised from the dead
statement: Paul taught that God has appointed a day in which he will judge the world in righteousness by the man he has ordained, giving assurance to all in that he has raised him from the dead.

label: The Areopagus hearers were divided: some mocked, some wanted to hear again
statement: When the hearers heard of the resurrection of the dead, some mocked; but others said, 'We want to hear you again concerning this.'

label: Dionysius the Areopagite, Damaris and others believed at Athens
statement: Certain men joined Paul and believed, among whom was Dionysius the Areopagite, and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.
note: Dionysius and Damaris are known only from this verse; the later bishop-of-Athens tradition and the Pseudo-Dionysius corpus are reception.
